cards.text: John is writing a letter to believers he calls his little children. He's just told them that when anyone sins, Jesus Christ is their advocate before the Father. Now he takes on a BIG question: how can you be SURE you've come to know Him?

cards.question: How does John say we can be sure we've come to know Him?

answers.text: If we feel close to Him
If we learn all about Him

cards.text: Now flip it. Somebody says, "I know Him," but doesn't keep His commandments, and that's me calling myself a world-famous baker with a COLD oven and zero cookies to show for it.

cards.question: Someone says, "I know Him," but doesn't keep His commandments. John says that person is a ___.
True or false: John says the truth is still in the person who claims to know Him but doesn't keep His commandments.

cards.text: But when someone keeps His word, John says something of God's is truly perfected in that person.

cards.question: If anyone keeps His word, the ___ of God has been truly perfected in him.

cards.text: Then John gives a way to know we're in Him. And just like with "I know Him," claiming it isn't enough.

cards.question: John says anyone who claims to abide in Him must walk a certain way. How?

cards.text: Not "talk about how Jesus walked," and not "nod real hard when somebody brings it up." WALK, friend, and I say that as a guy who has to HOP everywhere on a gold base.
Then John calls them "Beloved" and tells them about the commandment he's writing.

cards.question: True or false: John says the commandment he's writing is one they've had from the beginning.

cards.text: Then John turns right around and says he IS also writing them a new commandment. Old AND new, kind of like me: same old stamper from the junk drawer, made brand new.

cards.question: John calls the commandment new. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The true light is already shining
The last day has already come
The old law has been taken away

cards.text: Now somebody claims to be in the light, but hates his brother. I bet John's raising an eyebrow here, and with eyebrows like mine, friend, I KNOW that look.

cards.question: True or false: John says someone who claims to be in the light but hates his brother is on his way out of the darkness.
John says whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no cause of ___ in him.

cards.text: Then the flip side: whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and he doesn't know where he's going. Friend, I spent YEARS in a dark drawer, and I couldn't have found the scissors if they were sitting on my mustache.

cards.question: Whoever hates his brother doesn't know where he's going. Why not, according to John?

answers.text: The darkness has blinded his eyes
No one is showing him the way

cards.text: Next John speaks to his readers group by group: little children, fathers and young men. He gives each group a reason he's writing to them.

cards.question: John writes to the little children because their sins have been ___ through His name.
True or false: John writes to the fathers because they know Him who is from the beginning.
John writes to the young men because of something they've overcome. What is it?

cards.text: Then John switches to "I have written," tells the children they know the Father, and circles back to the fathers and the young men. That's me with every new baker at the oven: "It's hot. It's HOT. Friend, it is SO HOT."

cards.question: John tells the young men they are ___, and the word of God abides in them.

cards.text: Then John gets straight to the point, no small talk: do not love the world or anything in the world.

cards.question: If anyone loves the world, what does John say is not in him?

cards.text: John names what's in the world: the desires of the flesh, the desires of the eyes and the pride of life. And the desires of the eyes, friend, that's me staring down a fresh tray of chocolate chip cookies, swearing, "I'm just LOOKING."

cards.question: True or false: John says the desires of the flesh, the desires of the eyes and the pride of life come from the Father.

cards.text: Then John gives the long view: the world is passing away, along with its desires. Everything down here has an expiration date, just like the expired coupon I shared that drawer with, and bless him, he STILL believed in himself.

cards.question: The world is passing away. But John says someone remains forever. Who?

answers.text: Whoever does the will of God

findings.problem: The card says 'when anyone sins,' but 1 John 2:1 says 'if anyone does sin.' Changing 'if' to 'when' turns John's condition into a statement that sinning is certain.
The card names the writer as John with no introduction. The letter itself never names its writer. Its authorship comes from tradition, not from the text.
findings.question: For a letter that doesn't name its writer, like 1 John, should Papa Dorin name the traditional author and introduce him (for example, 'John, one of Jesus' twelve apostles')? Or should he say only 'the writer'? If he names him, what reference goes with it?

findings.problem: 'Somebody says, "I know Him,"' drops the 'If anyone' of 2:4. The hypothetical becomes a statement about a real person.

The joke compares the claim to Papa Dorin calling himself a world-famous baker with nothing to show for it. That frames the claim as a false one, which points straight to 'liar' on card 4 and rules out 'beginner' and 'stranger.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word in 'the ___ of God has been truly perfected.' Card 6 only says 'something of God's,' which gives nothing to reason from. 'Love,' 'power' and 'glory' are equally guessable, so this tests wording the baker hasn't seen.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card only restates 2:6, which was already told on card 8 and asked on card 9. It doesn't move the passage forward. It's a recap carrying a joke.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The question says 'the true light is already shining' is John's reason for calling the commandment new. In 2:8, 'For the darkness is fading...' follows 'which is true in Him and also in you,' so the text doesn't settle which statement the 'For' explains. The answer also drops 'the darkness is fading.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Now somebody claims to be in the light' drops the 'If anyone' of 2:9. The hypothetical becomes a statement about a real person.
The blank asks the baker to guess the exact wording in 'no cause of ___ in him.' No earlier card sets up stumbling, so 'stumbling,' 'sorrow' and 'shame' can't be reasoned out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'Everything down here has an expiration date' goes beyond 2:17, which says the world and its desires are passing away. The same verse says whoever does the will of God remains forever, so 'everything' says something the text shows is wrong.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
